Your rules file stays yours

PR playground for #4375: a SessionStart hook overwrote a tracked project rules file on every session.

src/hooks/src/prompt/antipattern-warning.ts writes a built-in anti-patterns list to .claude/rules/antipatterns.md so Claude Code loads it into every prompt. Before this PR it skipped the write only when the user-global copy was byte-identical to the template and the project copy was absent or identical. In every other case it wrote the template over the project file.

A project that tracked its own antipatterns.md lost its content on each session start, and a pull-based deploy checkout came back dirty every time, which blocked the next git pull.

What the PR changes

FileChange
src/hooks/src/prompt/antipattern-warning.ts materializeAntipatternRules returns early when the project file exists, so it seeds only an absent file. It still skips seeding when the user-global copy is byte-identical, and ORK_NO_RULE_SEED=1 turns seeding off entirely.
src/hooks/src/__tests__/prompt/antipattern-warning.test.ts Four new cases: a git-indexed project copy survives with no global copy, an identical one and a different one, and the opt-out skips seeding. The old "refreshes a stale project copy" test is reversed to "preserves".
Trade-off, accepted in #4375: a project copy seeded by an older ork version is no longer refreshed when the built-in template changes. Delete the file to get a fresh seed.
